cases.note: Bare identifier. Agrees under both readings — control.
Control: the common deny case must not regress.
Bare * survives id-scope. The shipped open-grants seed uses operations:["*"]; a strict string-equality reading would break bootstrap.
Trailing /* = literal segment-prefix, the second and last surviving wildcard.
The prefix retains its slash, so a longer first segment does not match.
prefix = pattern minus the trailing '*' = 'compute/', and 'compute' does not start with 'compute/'. Same boundary as §5.4.
F40 HEADLINE (include over-grant). A canonicalizing peer ALLOWS this; the conformant reading denies it. /*/ is not an interior wildcard in id-scope.
No peer-relative qualification in id-scope: the value is never rewritten to /{local}/get.
No leading-/ universal reading. Agrees under both readings, but pins the rule.

Control: the §3.6 default (peers absent -> local only) must still deny a foreign peer.
F40 (include over-grant), peers dimension. The divergence is not operations-only.
F40 (include over-grant), peers dimension, absolute-qualified form.
PRECISION: path syntax in an id dimension is matched literally, NOT rejected. A value that IS that literal string matches. Peers must not add a validation error for path syntax here.
Control: an exclude that agrees under both readings still denies.

F40 HEADLINE (exclude inversion) — the single highest-value case. A canonicalizing peer DENIES; the conformant reading ALLOWS, because the exclude pattern matches nothing literally. A peer cannot pass this by accident, and a rejection-only oracle probe would never surface it.
The exclude inversion on the peers dimension.
The surviving trailing-/* wildcard still works on the exclude side.
path-scope CONTROL: canonicalization is retained. Both sides -> /{local}/system/tree.
path-scope CONTROL: the /*/ interior peer-wildcard MUST still work here. This is what proves the fix is a SPLIT, not a blanket removal of canonicalization.
path-scope CONTROL: trailing /* after canonicalization.
path-scope CONTROL, exclude side: still canonicalizes, so the exclude still bites. Mirror of id.exclude.pathform — together they prove the two matchers are genuinely distinct.
